verdict: Chubb earned $2.8B as record investment income and disciplined underwriting — an 84.1% combined ratio — more than covered catastrophe losses that were two and a half times last year's unusually light level.

kpis.note: operating revenue, vs a year ago

kpis.note: underwriting kept $15.90 of every $100 of premium

segments.name: Net premiums earned
segments.note: Premiums from property & casualty and life policies, earned over the coverage period — up 3.9%. Consolidated net premiums written were $15.1B, up 1.9%.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the money Chubb invests between collecting premiums and paying claims — a record quarter, helped by rising interest rates.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.note: Other income of $388M, less a $24M loss on separate-account assets held for policyholders.

otherDetail: Net realized losses of $455M on investments and $65M of market risk benefits losses, partly offset by $108M of losses attributable to noncontrolling interests (borne by others, not Chubb shareholders) — a net $412M drag shown in the chart.
oneTimers: Pre-tax catastrophe losses were $705M, versus an unusually light $285M a year ago — the main reason core operating income fell 2.2% despite growth elsewhere.
Favorable prior-period development of $511M: reserves set aside for past claims proved more than enough, so $511M flowed back into profit (vs $361M a year ago).
Net realized losses of $455M on the investment portfolio are included in GAAP net income but excluded from Chubb's headline core operating income of $2,980M ($7.66 per share, non-GAAP).

takeaways.title: Underwriting stayed disciplined
takeaways.text: The P&C combined ratio of 84.1% means claims and expenses took 84 cents of every premium dollar. Excluding catastrophes, the current-accident-year ratio was 82.6%, and P&C underwriting income was $2.1B.

takeaways.title: Investments set a record
takeaways.text: Adjusted net investment income was a record $1.89B (GAAP net investment income $1.79B, +9%), as higher interest rates lift what Chubb earns on premiums held before claims are paid.

takeaways.title: Catastrophes explain the dip
takeaways.text: Catastrophe losses of $705M were 2.5 times last year's light $285M. That is why core operating income eased 2% in the quarter even though the nine-month figure is a record $8.6B, up 21%.

footerNote: Chubb does not print a single total-revenue line that fits this chart: revenue here is premiums earned plus net investment income plus other operating income ($17,079M). Net realized losses and market risk benefits losses are shown below operating income in Other income, and net income is the $2,844M attributable to Chubb (consolidated net income was $2,736M after a $108M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests).
